explanation: Rotate each concentric layer through four-way exchanges. Save the four corresponding cells, then move bottom-left to top-left, bottom-right to bottom-left, top-right to bottom-right, and top-left to top-right.
timeComplexity: O(n²): Θ(n²) cells take part in constant-sized exchanges. Every cell moves a constant number of times and no second matrix is allocated.
spaceComplexity: O(1): only indices and four saved values are needed. All exchanges occur within existing rows, using only a constant number of temporary values.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/matrix_rotation.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Each exchange maps every participating original position (r,c) to (c,n−1−r). The layer loops cover each noncentral cell in exactly one four-cycle, so the whole matrix rotates clockwise without overwriting an unsaved value.
walkthrough: For [[1,3],[5,7]], the one four-cycle moves 1 to top-right, 3 to bottom-right, 7 to bottom-left, and 5 to top-left. The matrix becomes [[5,1],[7,3]]. JSON arguments are [matrix]. The observed output is the mutated matrix, including for native callables whose return type is void/None.
edgeCases: No replacement rows or second matrix are needed.
